statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-48978 (GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, GO-2026-5885): the oras-go auth client follows the realm URL in a registry Bearer challenge without validating its scheme or host, so a malicious or compromised registry can direct the token request, with the stored credentials, to an internal address or over plain http (auth Client.Do). Affected is oras.land/oras-go/v2 before 2.6.1. Refs: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, fix https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/7a9f4b0b9558821b0422152ebe21ae56930fe764, release https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/releases/tag/v2.6.1, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5885. Checked every scout-cli-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to 1.30.0-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each holds /usr/bin/docker-scout, the Docker Scout CLI Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 for GOOS=linux; the -dev build has the same Go release and module versions as the scout-cli build of the same version, built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath. We read the Go build information (module versions and replace directives) of every build from the published packages, and re-read the 1.26.0-r3 scout-cli x86_64 and 1.20.4-r1 scout-cli-dev aarch64 Alpine 3.23 packages ourselves (checksums equal to the index). The relevant module is oras-go v2.6.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0; oras-go v2.6.2 in 1.23.1-r1 to 1.30.0-r1. No published build carries oras-go 2.6.1. So the builds before 1.23.1-r1 carry oras-go 2.6.0, before the fixed 2.6.1, and 1.23.1-r1 and every later build carry 2.6.2, which includes the 2.6.1 fix. In the function tables of the two builds we re-read ourselves, registry/remote/auth.(*Client).Do is linked.

Refs: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, fix https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/7a9f4b0b9558821b0422152ebe21ae56930fe764, release https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/releases/tag/v2.6.1, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5885. The scout-cli-fips-dev packages are built from the same Docker Scout CLI source with Go FIPS 140-3 mode enabled and are published in the DHI security repository, not in the repository we read for the other owners. CVE-2026-48978 (GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, GO-2026-5885): the oras-go auth client follows the realm URL in a registry Bearer challenge without validating its scheme or host, so a malicious or compromised registry can direct the token request, with the stored credentials, to an internal address or over plain http (auth Client.Do). Affected is oras.land/oras-go/v2 before 2.6.1. Refs: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, fix https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/7a9f4b0b9558821b0422152ebe21ae56930fe764, release https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/releases/tag/v2.6.1, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5885. Checked every scout-cli package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to 1.30.0-1, each for amd64 and arm64. Each package lists one file in its md5sums, /usr/bin/docker-scout, the Docker Scout CLI Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 for GOOS=linux. That program is the same file as in the Alpine 3.23 scout-cli build of the same version and architecture (1.20.4-r1 for 1.20.4-1, and so on): each pair has the same Go build ID, which embeds a hash of the linked program. We read the Go build information (module versions and replace directives) of every build from the published packages, and re-read the 1.26.0-r3 scout-cli x86_64 and 1.20.4-r1 scout-cli-dev aarch64 Alpine 3.23 packages ourselves (checksums equal to the index). The relevant module is oras-go v2.6.0 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-0; oras-go v2.6.2 in 1.23.1-1 to 1.30.0-1. No published build carries oras-go 2.6.1. So the builds before 1.23.1-1 carry oras-go 2.6.0, before the fixed 2.6.1, and 1.23.1-1 and every later build carry 2.6.2, which includes the 2.6.1 fix. In the function tables of the two builds we re-read ourselves, registry/remote/auth.(*Client).Do is linked.
